There exists $\epsilon _0>0$ such that for all $0<\epsilon \le \epsilon _0$ the following is true. Suppose that $N$ and $N'$ are $\epsilon $-necks centered at $x$ and $x'$, respectively, in a Riemannian manifold $M$. Suppose that $x'$ is not contained in $N$ but is contained in the closure of $N$ in $M$. Suppose also that the two-spheres of the neck structure on $N$ and $N'$ separate $M$. Then, possibly after reversing the $\epsilon $-neck structures on $N$ and/or $N'$, the pair $\{ N,N'\} $ forms a balanced chain.

\label{firstchain}

There exists $\epsilon_0>0$ such that for all $0<\epsilon\le
\epsilon_0$ the following is true.  Suppose that $N$ and $N'$ are
$\epsilon$-necks centered at $x$ and $x'$, respectively, in a
Riemannian manifold $M$. Suppose that $x'$ is not contained in $N$
but is contained in the closure of $N$ in $M$. Suppose also that the
two-spheres of the neck structure on $N$ and $N'$ separate $M$.
Then, possibly after reversing the $\epsilon$-neck structures on $N$
and/or $N'$, the pair $\{N,N'\}$ forms a balanced chain.
\end{lemma}
